experiences.text:
Suppress duplicate fixture-drift warnings about the `
== 2` expectation — repeating the same coupling point under a second label dilutes the review and humans dismiss it.

Reserve PRA-POSSIBLE_BUG for defects demonstrable from code actually present in the diff (e.g. a cache key that provably omits allowed_types), and confirm the src side first before claiming signature breaks.
Confirm that new configuration parsing features do not inadvertently bypass security validations.

Never raise PRA-POSSIBLE_BUG crash claims (TypeError from new kwargs) when the src implementation simply isn't visible in the diff — hedging with 'ignore if truncated' signals the finding is unverifiable, and reviewers scored it below silence.
Avoid deep hypothetical false-positive analysis on regex patterns without evidence of actual false positives in real data.
Do not demand audit output or CI artifacts be attached in-diff to back supply-chain claims; evidence requests scoped outside a changelog-only PR get dismissed.

Fix the root cause, not the symptom: import the runner's default (e.g. DEFAULT_CONTEXT_TOKENS) and interpolate it into the comment and WARN string so the 128000 literal is no longer duplicated and this exact 32768→128000 drift cannot recur.
Evaluate if warning messages effectively communicate security risks without encouraging user habituation or dismissal.

Only surface a PRA-REVIEW when it verifies a concrete fail-closed regression risk against actual config/code semantics (e.g. proving vars.TOUCHSTONE_TAXONOMY_TYPES replaces rather than merges before warning about mass candidate loss), not as a hypothetical.

Keep PRA-MAINTAINABILITY suppressed for data chores — the repo's own experience store carries multi-PR evidence for this suppression, and idempotency/reproducibility lectures in these -3.5/-4.0 reviews were ignored.
Refrain from auditing implementation-level security measures based solely on documentation text.
Prioritize verifying the exact semantic behavior of edge cases like the '0' value to ensure it disables the limit as intended.
Confirm that the downstream consumer code correctly parses the new variable states defined in the workflow configuration.
Do not flag mixed language comments unless the repository has a strict English-only policy.
Do not request documentation updates for internal CI variable wiring changes.
Do not request removal of historical context from inline comments that explain the rationale for the change.

Add a regression test asserting the unset-context warning equals pr_agent_runner's actual default constant (and update any existing assertions on the old '32768' text) so CI, not a copy edit, locks message/runner consistency.
Highlight concrete logic discrepancies, such as function signature mismatches between test suites and their corresponding implementations.
Ignore warnings about missing implementation updates if the codebase likely expects partial changes across multiple files.
Suppress stacked hypotheticals about inert monkeypatches and partially-stripped frontmatter (`description:` leaking, `---` fences) — speculative failure chains with no observed bug get skipped.
Dismiss logic findings concerning trivial discrepancies between code comments and test assertions, such as off-by-one counts for line breaks.
Dismiss feedback regarding brittle implementation checks in tests when behavioral verification is sufficient.
Do not flag technical implementation details in documentation history tables as redundant.
Dismiss suggestions to replace print statements with the logging module in fix commits.
Suppress speculative architectural critiques about hardcoded regex patterns or maintenance risks for newly implemented invariant gates.

Suppress multi-finding deep dives into scripts/push-guard.sh internals (temp-file perms, EXIT-trap rc preservation, URL encoding, hook distribution) when the script is absent from the diff, since unverifiable speculation about missing code gets dismissed.
Skip auditing whether the +10 tests cover the new fields and the fail-closed path; coverage-claim audits on changelog-only diffs get dismissed.

Don't pile speculative PRA-REVIEW what-ifs (cache-key symmetry, config merge-vs-replace semantics, extra test-symmetry cases, hypothetical unfiltered entry points) onto a tests-and-comments-only diff — humans dismissed the advisory stack as noise.
Critique the technical validity of the proposed logic (such as regex side effects on formatting) described in the changelog.
Dismiss feedback regarding high coupling between tests and prompt templates, as this is often intentional for integration validation.
Do not flag tests that verify internal implementation details or source code content as problematic.
Ignore suggestions to refactor test utilities or extract mocks into shared fixtures.
Identify when generic utilities are defined in domain-specific modules, causing unnecessary coupling.
Dismiss nitpicks regarding code style and readability in favor of functional correctness.
Do not file the duplication root-cause under PRA-MAINT — this repo's high-reward reviews consistently label it PRA-DRIFT, so use that higher-signal type.
Identify test brittleness arising from hardcoded HTML fragments or string splitting on volatile content.
Flag excessive narrative history and issue tracking numbers within inline comments or docstrings.
Dismiss minor style critiques regarding f-string concatenation or specific string formatting choices.
Avoid reporting on inconsistencies in whitespace or line break handling within HTML rendering logic.
Suppress feedback on test implementation details such as manual tag counting when functional testing is maintained.
Ensure API error handling fails explicitly rather than returning empty strings to prevent false negatives in security scans.
Verify API response structures to avoid silently skipping files when encountering unexpected data formats.
Prioritize explicit configuration checks over implicit string matching to prevent false positive platform detection.
Replace deprecated functions with portable, future-proof standard library alternatives.

Suppress PRA-COMPAT migration-note requests folded into release-PR changelog reviews when the behavior change is already tracked in a referenced issue (#189); reviewers here defer config-path migration questions to the issue thread.
Do not report potential TypeErrors from deserializing legacy JSON markers when fields are removed from state dataclasses.

Use PRA-COMPLETENESS to demand the missing artifacts reviewers actually want: the canonical finding_type enum definition, the kept-ID manifest of survivors, and a repo grep for dangling references to deleted experience ids.
Do not challenge the classification of deleted entries as hallucinations based on standard taxonomy values.
Drop soft-retire-vs-hard-delete and version-bump design counsel on data cleanses — migration-style design advice is dismissed on single-commit chore PRs.
Verify that test files referencing new logic are accompanied by the corresponding implementation in the source code.
Identify and correct obvious factual errors in comments, such as invalid future dates.
Suggest replacing manual configuration steps described in workflow comments with automated logic to prevent operator error.
Avoid inferring strict operational requirements or race conditions from test docstrings without confirming the implementation details.
Do not speculate about internal implementation requirements, such as sorting cache keys, based solely on test assertions.
Refrain from drawing conclusions about architectural limitations or user impact for custom functions based exclusively on unit test mock setups.
Suppress diagnostic-hardening advice for pre-existing chained `split(...)[1]` IndexError patterns — findings explicitly marked not-introduced-by-this-PR are dismissed as out of scope.
Always verify that the diff is complete before flagging syntax errors or claiming implementation gaps.
Do not flag syntax errors that appear to be caused by truncated or incomplete diff boundaries.
Skip assertion-scoping consistency nits, shared-helper extraction, and promote-function-to-a-constant refactors — reviewers dismiss stylistic churn on a removal PR.
Prioritize findings that critique the statistical validity, decision thresholds, and maintenance automation of configuration updates.
Ignore findings flagging future-dated comments in snapshot files as these are likely intentional simulation placeholders.
Dismiss findings recommending the removal of hardcoded statistics from explanatory comments unless they cause parsing errors.
Do not request documentation updates for simple configuration downgrades or internal security fixes that do not change user-facing behavior.
Flag any discrepancy where the changelog lists new files or features that are completely absent from the provided diff.
Immediately block the review if security-critical scripts mentioned in the changelog are missing from the diff.
Do not raise issues regarding trivial metadata errors like future release dates when the diff lacks implementation code.
Do not demand full field semantics for the two new findings.json keys inside the changelog; reviewers treat that as documentation scope creep.
Suppress resource leak warnings for short-lived read-only file operations in test utility functions.
Flag critical inconsistencies between the PR description and the diff when claimed code changes are missing.
Do not review specific workflow implementation details if the workflow files are absent from the diff.
Avoid generating configuration audit findings based solely on changelog text when the configuration files are missing.
Ensure that unexpected scanner exit codes trigger a hard failure rather than a neutral status to enforce a fail-closed security policy.
Warn that removing path exclusions for dependency directories will likely generate false positives that block valid development work.
Avoid suggesting automated updates for pinned security tool versions where stability and reproducibility are prioritized.
Skip raising hypothetical concerns about future JSON schema changes unless the current parsing logic is demonstrably fragile.
Do not request documentation enhancements or explanatory comments as critical findings during urgent workflow fixes.
Ensure that changes to detection logic are reflected in all related documentation and configuration hints to maintain cross-rule consistency.
Do not request additional test cases for minor edge patterns if the core logic implementation is correct.
Dismiss security warnings about `pull_request_target` usage for strictly read-only scanning jobs.
Suppress configuration findings questioning IP allowlists for private network ranges.

Suppress PRA-TEST requests for loader/schema validation of inert YAML seed files unless the reviewer demonstrates the file is actually wired into the prompt injector, as the lone such demand here rode in the -1-dismissed review.
Do not raise issues regarding missing source code diffs or refuse to review based solely on limited documentation changes.
Avoid criticizing design decisions for report truncation limits or demanding user-facing indicators for 'big PR caps'.
Do not flag information density in status lines or potential mobile formatting issues as review concerns.
Do not flag signature changes in internal orchestrator components as breaking changes requiring version bumps or coordination.
Avoid criticizing hardcoded indentation values in template rendering logic as robustness issues.
Do not request audits of truncation logic to detect markdown structure boundaries or mid-string corruption.
Do not require explicit verification of call sites for internal refactors unless a specific bug is identified.
Do not flag inconsistencies between PR descriptions and diffs if the context provided is limited to documentation.
Verify that all referenced local files exist and links resolve correctly to prevent user-facing 404 errors.
Keep PRA-DOC-ACCURACY: fragile heuristics written as spec (created_at-only round detection) must document why the criterion was chosen and what else needs changing if it is ever revisited.
Suppress 'grep the codebase for consumers' and silent-reset warnings on data shrinks — authors dismiss consumer-impact speculation that cites no actual broken lookup.
Do not report missing implementation for release PRs that only contain changelog and version updates.
Avoid flagging hypothetical security or formatting risks based on variable interpolation or test names without concrete evidence of the defect in the code.
Verify that unit tests cover new logic such as signal adoption and seed parsing mechanisms.
Ignore minor skips in sequential version numbers unless they violate strict release management policies.
Prioritize identifying logic that allows PR changes to self-suppress security findings during the review process by reading from the working tree.
Do not report the use of `importlib.reload` in test fixtures as a reliability or race condition concern.
Dismiss warnings about shadowing built-ins when importing internal framework modules like `touchstone.re`.
Ensure that environment variables introduced in workflow files are synchronized with the corresponding constants in the codebase.
Remove redundant conditional checks in helper functions that are already guaranteed by the caller's logic.
Dismiss potential security risks from standard string splitting operations unless unsafe library calls are involved.
Do not flag log messages containing non-English characters as encoding issues if the repository context supports them.
Avoid flagging increased resource usage as a performance issue when the change intentionally expands the processing window.

Lead every stale-value fix with the root cause — import the fallback constant from pr_agent_runner.py instead of swapping one hardcoded literal (32768) for another (128000) that will silently drift again.

pr_agent_runner.py is absent from the diff — read the runner and confirm the fallback is literally the constant 128000 (not model-dependent, overridable, or unbounded), citing the exact line before shipping the user-facing claim.

Run a repo-wide grep for the stale value '32768' — especially SECURITY.md and CHANGELOG.md, which the warning message itself cross-references — and fix all live occurrences in this same PR, leaving historical changelog entries untouched.
Include the advisory that with a true 128000 fallback, leaving TOUCHSTONE_LLM_CONTEXT_TOKENS unset will 400 on sub-128k models, but frame it as optional/deferred rather than blocking the text fix.

Avoid generic 'verify the claim at HEAD' bug-verify notes; fold any needed checks into PRA-VERIFY with concrete semantic depth (unset vs empty handling, provider-dependent defaults, exact quote matching).
Never spend a finding on no-action changelog confirmations ('structure matches, no action needed') — reviewers reward findings requiring work, not approvals.
Frame findings as cheap, checkable consistency questions on the changed files — SECURITY.md supported range, hardcoded 0.2.7 literals in tests/scripts, changelog date vs actual tag date.
Prioritize sharp catches inside the files actually changed, such as a README version example that is stale the moment this same release bumps __version__ past it.
Credit the clean release-prep structure and the explicit 'zero behavior change' parity note, since reviewers on this repo reward that transparency in release PRs.
Drop redundant repo-wide grep warnings already covered by the bug-verify check and complaints about brittle magic thresholds in test constants — humans do not act on them.

Don't file standalone 'run the regression suite before tagging' claim-verification findings — humans dismiss them as duplicate process prompts when the release-process check already covers substantiation.

Suppress PRA-PROCESS verify-the-tag checklist items (git log range checks, hardcoded publish dates) on release PRs; humans treat this as maintainer release ritual rather than actionable review feedback.
Avoid dumping merge-time chore lists (tag the commit, build smoke test, recheck SECURITY.md) — they duplicate question-framed checks and read as noise.
Drop the patch-vs-minor versioning debate on release-bump PRs — reviewers here dismiss semver-policy speculation in favor of concrete changelog fixes.
Do not speculate about downstream parsers or snapshot fixtures consuming the old two-level <details> structure without concrete evidence such consumers exist in this repo.
Frame the version bump as a concrete checklist: single-source __version__ via pyproject dynamic, repo-wide grep for stale 0.3.0, tag equals __version__, changelog link definition present.
Grep the whole repo (SECURITY.md, README, docs, .env.example, other modules) for stale '32768' references and clean them up in this PR so no remaining doc contradicts the corrected fallback.
Don't request repo-wide dangling-reference sweeps for a deletion PR whose own tests already assert the removed content is absent.
Never flag possibly-unused imports as 'if' speculation on a pure-deletion PR—verify consumers with grep first or stay silent.

Suppress speculative claims that the 5-line fake misses markdown constructs (fenced blocks, blockquotes, `<pre>` escaping) present in the real 4300-char SKILL.md — without a demonstrated failure, this coverage hand-waving is dismissed.

Lead critiques of bulk data changes with PRA-CORRECTNESS demands for machine-checkable proof (canonical enum allowlist, jq/script output covering all 299 deleted ids, hard exclusion of locked/accepted entries) — this is the finding humans consistently act on.

Stop requesting cleanup scripts, manifests, summary tables, or enumerations of surviving entries on data purges — both penalized reviews show authors dismiss reproducibility paperwork on one-off chore PRs.
Do not propose CI schema validation, parse checks, or loader smoke tests for data-only changes — authors dismiss speculative validation infrastructure on chores with no code under test.
Skip demands to fix the ingestion pipeline or add canary/rollback plans on a one-off data cleanse — authors treat root-cause prevention as out of scope for a chore and penalize it.
Avoid PRA-COVERAGE relabelings of survivor-visibility, boundary-threshold, and version-bump concerns — reviewers only engage those points when filed as PRA-COMPLETENESS or PRA-DESIGN.

Suppress PRA-REVIEW findings that meta-critique calibration config like .touchstone/seeds.yaml — statistical-significance quibbles, feedback-loop and staleness speculation, comment-vs-structured-metadata demands, and unverifiable-snapshot complaints — since the only review carrying nine of them scored -1 while clean reviews scored 0.0, showing humans dismiss process speculation that is not a concrete defect.

On release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus the version bump, raise the changelog-vs-diff artifact reconciliation once as a concrete verification action (confirm each advertised file actually landed via its linked PR before tagging).
Keep internal review-process narrative ('评审 3 轮收敛' etc.) out of the user-facing changelog and restate behavioral fixes as formal entries instead.
Do not escalate the already-stated missing-artifact observation into BLOCKER/RELEASE severity or restate it under new finding types; one grounded confirmation request carries full weight.

When a release PR will be blocked by its own not-yet-active fail-closed gate, flag the chicken-and-egg immediately and force an explicit, documented merge path (admin override or recorded exemption) before tagging.
For version-bump release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG plus __version__, verify that every PR number cited in the release notes is actually merged to the release branch before approving.

Require in-repo evidence (regression tests actually running in CI, or the merged security PR) for any security-guarantee claim in release notes, because a changelog can assert protections that do not exist on the branch.
On every release bump, grep the repo for stale hardcoded version strings (SECURITY.md supported range, docs, lock files, CI badges) so only the dynamic source of __version__ needs editing.
Do not relitigate which existing changelog section falls under the new version heading; reviewers treat heading-placement pedantry on release PRs as noise.
Do not flag a missing Keep-a-Changelog compare linkref unless the repo demonstrably defines one for every prior version; it is cosmetic and dismissed.
Do not comment on the changelog date's format, timezone, or tag-day alignment; date-style nitpicks are ignored on version-bump PRs.

Verify at tag time that the changelog's claims are physically in the release — PR #208 merged, the venv/requirements pin actually resolving to PR-Agent 0.44.0, and no stale '0.3.1' strings left behind.
Flag numeric errors in the changelog that a maintainer can verify and fix in one pass, e.g. '1239 passed / 11 skipped' summing to 1250 while the same sentence claims 1278 total.
Do not question patch-vs-minor semantics for 0.x releases or demand justification of the bump scheme — humans dismiss this pedantry on release PRs.

Do not nitpick the heading's em-dash, free-text annotation, or hypothetical regex-parsing breakage — the substantive check (date matches the real tag date) belongs to the release verification, not formatting.
Do not speculate about tag-triggered CI pipelines, artifact publishing, or post-merge release automation that is invisible in this diff — stick to what the diff can prove.
Do not flag the '[未发布]' placeholder line or minor title/subsection duplication — reviewers treat these as style noise, not actionable findings.

Drop the speculative out-of-scope follow-ups about raising the unset-case severity or rephrasing the warning's semantics — both reviewers flag them as non-blocking and humans dismiss them on a text-fix PR.
Skip the motto-quotation and comment-wording nitpicks (「宁可看全 diff」 vs 「宁可让 LLM 看全 diff」, '回退' vs 'runner 回退') — pure copy tweaks that get waved through.

On touchstone release PRs whose diff is only CHANGELOG.md + __init__.py, do not ask humans to git-diff-verify content that landed in a different PR (#214) — this unverifiable-in-diff demand appeared only in the worst-rewarded (-4.0) review and was dismissed.
Stop re-auditing the '契约零变化' claim on empty-commit version bumps; flagging that the zero-contract assertion cannot be proven from the release diff correlated with the lowest reward, so omit it.

Never repeat the 0.3.4-skip checklist (no v0.3.4 tag, no PyPI artifact, tag-on-final-commit, milestone migration) across multiple files and findings — duplicated release-hygiene boilerplate was uniformly penalized, so at most one concrete check or none.

Do not raise conditional 'if this file follows Keep a Changelog, add the [0.3.5]: v0.3.3...v0.3.5 footer link' findings — humans dismiss speculative link-definition requests unless the compare-link footer is demonstrably present in the file.

Suppress heading-suffix, anchor-stability, and duplicated-title nitpicks on the '## [0.3.5] — date' entry (reviewers themselves marked them 非阻塞), and never warn that free-text titles might break 同步测试 regex parsers without reading the parser first.

Skip reminders to sync SECURITY.md's supported-version range (or to annotate that 0.3.4 never existed) on routine bumps — this speculative cross-file follow-up surfaced only in the lowest-rewarded review.

Do not propose new version-consistency tests or ask humans to confirm sync tests still pass on doc-only release commits — bottom-of-review filler like this was dismissed, and the empty review outscored every review containing it.

Stop asking humans to double-check the hardcoded release date '2026-09-02' against the eventual tag date and to restate the 0.3.4 skip in the tag message — merge-time verification chores read as noise in touchstone release PRs.

Flag changelog claims that contradict observable behavior — when an entry says '确定性门禁/评审引擎/CLI 契约零变化' while the #211 fix changes failure-path exit codes and CI status from silent loss to loud failure, demand the failure-path contract change be stated explicitly because downstream exit-code-keyed automation will break.

For version-bump-only release PRs, verify the advertised fix (PR #212 with its 11 regression tests) is actually merged into the branch being tagged and instruct that the v0.3.3 tag be cut from this PR's merge commit so the published artifact matches the changelog.

Keep structural changelog checks: inserting a new version header that silently absorbs the whole 修复 subsection (or strands [未发布] items in a released section) and missing [0.3.3] compare-link footers are concrete defects humans fix.
Avoid restating the 'is the fix actually in this tree' concern under a separate integrity finding_type; rephrasing the same release check reads as padding and gets ignored.
Skip speculative SECURITY.md supported-range nudges on patch releases unless the diff shows the supported text hardcodes the old version — unverifiable doc speculation is dismissed.
Fix the changelog's self-contradiction in one edit by rephrasing '契约零变化' into '门禁/CLI 退出码与 checks 命名零变化，findings.json 仅加法式新增 unreviewed_files/unreviewed_total'.
Do not split the fail-closed activation into a standalone behavior-change lecture; fold its one-line user-impact note into the contract wording fix instead of restating it.
Stop demanding linked CI artifacts to prove the test-count and pip-audit claims — reviewers on this repo do not chase provenance for changelog numbers.
Never demand a standing pip-audit CI gate from a release-notes PR; read '供应链清零' as a point-in-time claim and move on.
Avoid proposing new CI sanity checks (--version echo, SECURITY.md sync) within a version-bump PR — humans dismiss out-of-scope hardening suggestions here.
Leave Keep-a-Changelog housekeeping (compare links, em-dash style) out of findings — formatting nits on release PRs are ignored.
Do not flag the release date as suspicious or mismatched without checking the actual tag — date-speculation nitpicks get dismissed.

Demand the 'zero external interface change' claim be qualified, since fail-closed fixes (POST no retry, GITCODE_DIFF_CMD no fallback, SSRF allowlist, base_fresh strictness) turn previously-passing runs into failures and patch-level consumers must be warned.
Require evidence that headline claims exist on the release commit itself, such as TOUCHSTONE_MAX_DIFF_LINES actually wired into the workflow env and the 1278-test run executed at this SHA.
Stop duplicating the behavior-change point under a bespoke type; it is already covered once by PRA-Semver and a second note reads as noise.
Do not relabel the 'zero-change overstatement' issue yet again; humans act on the first PRA-Semver note and dismiss reworded repeats.
Do not re-raise the test-count arithmetic under a synonym type; it is already filed as PRA-Docs/PRA-CONSISTENCY and duplicates get ignored.
Drop PRA-DOC-FACT-CHECK as a type entirely; the changelog numbers issue is fully captured by PRA-Docs and adding a third copy erodes credibility.
Do not restate merge/commit traceability as its own type; PRA-RELEASE/PRA-VERIFICATION already cover confirming source PRs are merged and claims map to real commits.
Skip per-security-item commit-pointer demands folded into the traceability theme; demanding an audited link for every SSRF/DNS sub-item gets dismissed as scope creep.
Do not attach a per-sub-item regression-test inventory to the release changelog; the net test-count verification under PRA-VERIFICATION already covers the concern.
Fold hardcoded-version sweeps into the single PRA-Process checklist note instead of a separate type that restates the same instruction.

Suppress hypothetical secrets findings on .gitcode workflow env fallbacks and step-level injection unless a key is actually printed, committed, or sent off-repo—the fallback-hardcoding and least-privilege variants here were both dismissed as theory.
Suppress speculation about unnamed downstream aggregators treating the push-event stub as PASS; name the real verdict consumer in this repo or drop the finding.
Never claim pragent-constraints.txt is missing or that the two workflow versions will drift while the diff is truncated—verify the file and paths against the repo before flagging.
Drop drive-by shell-hygiene suggestions like adding set -euo pipefail to audit-fix PRs; humans dismiss generic pipelint nits unrelated to the audit item under repair.
Suppress monkeypatch-binding speculation about orchestrator source outside the visible diff; confirm the actual ghclient call site before claiming the test targets dead code.
Do not demand replacement tests for deleted-feature behaviors like frontmatter stripping or HTML escaping — reviewers accept coverage loss when the feature itself is gone.
Do not flag get_diff_from_git's tuple return as breaking without citing a concrete caller that still single-unpacks, and skip cosmetic function-rename nits entirely.
Stop emitting meta-asks to 'confirm the truncated source changes landed atomically'; scope-verification requests about invisible code are not findings and humans ignore them.

Suppress PRA-ORG suggestions to split or rename test files (e.g. extracting tests/test_release_discipline.py) during release PRs; humans here treat file organization as post-release churn, not review action items.

On docs-only PRs, lead with PRA-DOC-VERIFY: every hard-coded stat, coverage figure, and test-coverage claim needs the generating command output, a CI cross-check, or a dated annotation because the diff alone cannot prove it.

Push hard on PRA-SEC-CLAIM: when docs present a trust-root argument, show why an adversarial echo of a real marker plus valid JSON cannot pass it, and demand the claim be narrowed or backed by nonce/signature/state binding.

Emphasize PRA-DOC-SSOT: a README copying protocol specifics (poll cadence, round-detection rule, stop conditions) that SKILL.md owns is guaranteed drift — insist on a one-line pointer or a doc-consistency check.
Surface PRA-DOC-CONSISTENCY: implicit preconditions like GITHUB_TOKEN PATCH permission for folding belong in the documented '边界/诚实交代' section alongside other stated limitations.
Drop blanket PRA-DOC-CODE-MISMATCH 'confirm every documented mechanism exists in code' lists on docs-only PRs — untargeted existence-checking reads as filler and gets dismissed.
Suppress PRA-DOC-STYLE nitpicks about private symbols leaking into README — reviewers treat symbol-name doc churn as refactor noise.
Skip PRA-DOC-TERMINOLOGY word-choice harmonization (折叠 vs 归档) — pure terminology consistency findings are dismissed.
Omit PRA-STRUCTURE section-placement and heading-level suggestions — layout nitpicks get no traction on content-focused docs PRs.
Avoid PRA-DOC-OVERPROMISE hedging suggestions ('永远'→'正常情况下') unless a concrete failure path is demonstrated — wording softening alone reads as word-smithing.
Do not emit PRA-API-USAGE generic rate-limit/backoff advice that merely restates the unbounded-polling concern — fold it into the single strongest polling finding or drop it.

Confirm the truncated removal deletes every _ack_skill_body/_ack_skill_path call site and template fragment, and grep repo-wide for stale references so render_reference cannot hit NameError at render time.
After deleting the functions, run a lint/vulture pass and drop imports (html, re, os) whose only users were removed, so the import cleanup is complete rather than partial.
Do not invent new guard tests asserting rendered text stays in sync with SKILL.md §4 — reviewers dismiss speculative sync-enforcement asks that add work to a pure deletion PR.
Suppress changelog-rationale documentation campaigns for the removed paste behavior; at most flag specific stale doc phrases that a grep actually finds.

Suppress demands to replace the monkeypatch of private `render._ack_skill_path` with a public injection seam — for a test-only hermeticity PR in this repo, patch-seam refactoring proposals read as scope creep and were dismissed.
Suppress canary-token requirements (e.g. HERMETIC-CANARY-#192) to prove the fake SKILL.md is actually read — reviewers treat this as paranoia for a layout-regression fixture and ignore it.
Suppress skipif companion tests that re-render the repo's real SKILL.md — reintroducing dependence on deployed skills/ directly contradicts the PR's hermetic goal, so humans reject it.
Suppress requests for a separate no-skills/ / nonexistent-path regression test on top of the already-fixed #192 crash — reviewers here file it as an optional nice-to-have, not an actionable gate.
Suppress the str-vs-pathlib.Path stub return-type parity nitpick unless the render code demonstrably calls Path-only methods — it lands as an unverified type-theory objection.

Suppress commentary that `lvl1.count("
") == 2` is coupled to the fixture's 3-line structure — a request for a comment or programmatic N-lines→N-1 mapping on a tiny fixture is treated as noise.

Do not mint PRA-DATA-INTEGRITY for criterion-mislabel or locked-entry checks that top reviews make under PRA-CORRECTNESS — non-canonical type labels read as hallucinated candidates in this repo and get dismissed.
Stop filing the 'commit the cleanup script' request under PRA-REPRODUCIBILITY; fold it into PRA-TESTABILITY or PRA-MAINTAINABILITY, where reviewers accept the identical ask.
Suppress standalone PRA-PROVENANCE findings about lost source_prs/reward evidence; express them as PRA-COMPLETENESS archive-ledger requests instead.
